findings.text: WindowNavigator:_replace ignores the boolean returned by _removeTop. If the removed window's Clear/destroy/pool-release cleanup fails, replacement still commits and opens the prepared candidate and can return Success. The approved cleanup contract requires the operation to return CleanupFailed whenever any cleanup/destroy/release step fails while keeping stack recovery committed; this is reachable with the same failing-Clear fixture already used for ordinary close.

A successful Open releases its transition input-block handle inside _transition before _add publishes ui.window.opened. The approved Add flow requires the applied opened confirmation first and transition-handle release afterward, so listeners/focus can observe the window as already unblocked before its opened confirmation.

WindowHandle.new returns a mutable table even though the approved handle contract requires an immutable generation witness. A normal caller can overwrite WindowId, _navigator, _registration, _generation, or _cast, causing public handle methods to throw or query altered authority instead of returning the specified generation-safe result.

WindowNavigationRegistry detects duplicate authored overrides with tostring(override.From) plus Direction. Roblox Instance tostring values are name-based, so two distinct eligible controls with the same Name and direction collide and valid navigation configuration is rejected, despite the requirement defining duplicates by exact From instance and direction.

UiSystemTestRunner labels a short happy-path stack scenario as TS-TEST-004/005/008 but does not observe lifecycle events or Pause/Resume hooks, and has no required deterministic Pause/Resume exception/yield fixtures or close/replacement failure ordering partitions. It therefore cannot prove the explicit current-slice ordering and recovery requirements and would not catch the transition-release or replacement-cleanup defects above; this is a required SLICE-003 verification gap, not a request for broader Cartesian testing.
